newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Spain truckers stop GM Hungary engine output.
newsitem.headline: Spain truckers stop GM Hungary engine output.

text.p: Engine production at the Hungarian plant of German automaker Adam Opel AG, a subsidiary of the U.S. General Motors was halted on Wednesday due to lack of components from Spain, currently hit by a truckers' strike.
"From today production at our engine plant is temporarily interrupted due to the continued truck drivers' blockade in Spain," Opel Hungary Ltd spokesman Zoltan Kaszas told Reuters.
Kaszas said the car assembly operation of Opel Astras and the company's cylinder head plant is not affected for the time being as there are sufficient components in store.
"The problem is twofold," he said. "We are missing incoming material from Spain and we cannot ship ready engines to Opel plants in Germany, as they have also stopped production."
He added that the company planned to resume normal production -- current 1,700 engines a day -- from Monday. "We certainly hope the problem will be resolved by then," he said.
Kaszas said lost production would be made up through overtime and Saturday working.
"We intend to compensate time lost at some later occasion but this will of course incur extra costs to the company in overtime payments," he said.
Kaszas added that if the Spanish truckers' strike is not resolved by the weekend "further measures will be necessary" but declined to specify what these measures would be.
Opel Hungary Ltd, launched in 1992, inaugurated last September new operations that double its engine production capacity to 460,000 units a year.
The additional units -- a variety of 1.4 litre and 1.6 litre Ecotec engines -- are exported to GM's car assembly plants around the world.

Along with the increase in engine production the company decided last year to reduce its car output to 11,100 units in 1996 from 12,488 units the year before, due to continuing adverse effects of the Hungarian government's austerity program on the country's car market.
Since it opened in 1992, Opel has invested over 700 million marks ($415.3 million) in its Hungarian operation.
